lead.en: Saphan Khwai is the working corridor between Ari's cafe rows and the Chatuchak market edge: BTS N7 over a wide, fast Phahonyothin Road, Pradiphat Road as the dense food spine, Or Tor Kor market at the unit's north-west corner, and 39 bars still pouring past 9 pm. Rents run below the app's Phaya Thai blend at station-adjacent buildings (12,000-23,000 baht studios and one-beds captured), while the two-bed blend of 36,500 matches district ranges. The frictions: 'almost no green space' by the neighbourhood guide's own account, a road you can only cross at spaced points, early closing by southern-Bangkok standards, and a safety score with no unit-specific evidence behind it.

strengths.en: Density of everyday food and drink: 175 restaurants and 149 cafés in the neighbourhood dataset, a named food spine on Pradiphat Road, and premium daily shopping at Or Tor Kor at the unit's edge.
Value rents with boardable rush-hour trains: station-adjacent one-beds captured at 12,000-23,000 baht, below the district blend, and morning trains you can actually board.

tradeoffs.en: The road dominates: wide, fast, viaduct-noisy, crossable only at spaced points, with no centre — 'an intersection, not a square'.
Green and late hours are thin: 'almost no green space' (Chatuchak Park 'a trip, not a stroll'), closing earlier than Ari, and no park centroid within 850 m in OSM.

dayNight.en: Mornings start before 7 am around the markets; evenings wind down by Ari's standards — 163 of 445 timed places still open at 9 pm, 39 bars past 9 pm, and post-midnight movement by taxi or motorbike taxi once BTS stops.

variation.en: The west side (Pradiphat band, market approaches) carries the density; the east side beyond the railway is the quiet residential pocket (Saliratthawiphak), and the south fringe toward Ari holds most of the 2 am bars.

fit.en: Fit for value-seeking renters and food-first residents who accept road noise and early closing; the hostels and craft-beer arrivals suit a young, mobile crowd.
Poor fit for green-space daily users and late-night rail commuters — the park is a trip, not a stroll, and the BTS stops before the last bars do.

uncertainties: Nightlife count basis: app 15 venues vs the neighbourhood dataset's 49 bars in a wider 1.2 km boundary — polygon decides (saphan-khwai-c06).
The app's 0.7 ha mapped park has no identified OSM counterpart; green 6 may be generous (saphan-khwai-c08).
Safety 8 has no unit-specific evidence in any read source (saphan-khwai-c11).
App anchor 13.7914 vs OSM station node 13.79382 — reconcile as unit centroid vs node (saphan-khwai-c01).
Primary station article is a flagged unsourced stub; ridership figure uncorroborated.

limitations: Underlying article is unsourced; ridership figure not corroborated by a second read source.
Counts cover food/drink/personal-services places, not all amenities (the site says services categories are too thin to count honestly).
Dataset excludes most services and vendors inside markets; venue longevity not verified.
The app's 15 nightlife venues cannot be reconciled to the site's 49-bar boundary figure without the polygon; venue hours change often per the source.
HipFlat averages in USD without stated conversion; Superagent is content-marketing with anecdotal figures.
OSM completeness for small pocket parks is imperfect; a 0.7 ha parcel could exist untagged or tagged differently.
Hours are business-listing data that the source says change often.
2021 ridership reflects COVID-era levels; relative ranking more meaningful than absolutes.
Safety 8 unverified — no crime data or resident reports accessible (Reddit/TripAdvisor 403 per brief); travel guide undated.
